summary: The bill requires U.S. Customs and Border Protection to automatically refund within 90 days all tariffs collected under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act on imports since January 1, 2025, by liquidating or reliquidating affected entries without requiring importers to file claims.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates that CBP issue refunds of tariffs collected under IEEPA. These refunds constitute government outlays (disbursements from the Treasury), which expands government spending relative to keeping the collected revenue. The effect is direct but secondary to the trade purpose, so the magnitude is small.

Tariffs are taxes on imports. The bill requires automatic refund of all IEEPA-imposed tariffs collected since January 1, 2025, without protest or application. This directly reduces the tax burden on importers and is therefore a tax reduction measure.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare delivery, insurance, public programs, or market regulation.
No provisions address firearms, ammunition, or gun regulations.
Although CBP is the implementing agency, the bill addresses only tariff refunds and does not alter immigration enforcement, visas, asylum, or border policy.
No provisions relate to reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions affect defense budgets, military procurement, or national security spending.
No provisions address environmental regulations, emissions, or climate policy.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.
No provisions relate to schools, student aid, or education funding.
No provisions address controlled substances, enforcement, or decriminalization.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal procedure.

The bill's sole purpose is to refund tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. By mandating automatic, retroactive refunds of these duties, the legislation directly reverses protectionist tariff measures and moves policy toward freer trade and reduced barriers.

Refunding collected tariffs reduces government revenue and increases the deficit. While this has a fiscal consequence, the bill does not articulate any debt-reduction or deficit-acceptance strategy; the debt impact is incidental.
No provisions address LGBTQ legal protections or discrimination.
No provisions address foreign assistance programs or funding.
No provisions relate to voting access, election administration, or campaign finance.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or platform oversight.
No provisions address collective bargaining, worker protections, or union rules.
No provisions address religious exemptions or civil-rights enforcement.
